key_insight: PI-MFA embeds PDE, boundary, and initial-condition physics into B-spline reconstruction so continuous flow fields are both smooth and physically consistent.
engineering_relevance: It gives engineers a compact, differentiable surrogate for flow data that improves downstream analysis, visualization, and derived quantities when measurements or simulations are inconsistent.
method: Tensor-product B-splines build a continuous multivariate field with local support.
Control points are optimized to balance data fit against PDE residuals and boundary/initial constraints.
Exact analytic spline derivatives make residual evaluation efficient without storing full-resolution fields.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical tests on 1D convection-diffusion, 2D coupled Burgers, and 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes cases, showing lower PDE residuals, improved balance-law consistency, and better errors than standard/regularized MFA, with computational advantages over tested PINNs.
watch_item: Performance depends on the chosen PDE constraints and data quality, so overly strong or mismatched physics terms may bias the reconstruction.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed B-Spline Framework for Continuous Approximation of Flow Data
